```{r setup, include=FALSE}
reporting_ready <- requireNamespace("gtsummary", quietly = TRUE) &&
  utils::packageVersion("gtsummary") >= "2.6.1"
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = reporting_ready)
```

```{r optional-packages, echo=FALSE, results='asis', eval=!reporting_ready}
cat("Install gtsummary version 2.6.1 or later to run these reporting examples. Estimation with cifmodeling does not require gtsummary.")
```

## A cumulative incidence table

The `diabetes.complications` dataset is the anonymized cohort used in the
package overview. Follow-up is measured in years; event 1 is diabetic
retinopathy and event 2 is a macrovascular complication. This example reports
retinopathy probabilities by fruit-intake group.

```{r first-table}
library(cifmodeling)
library(gtsummary)
data(diabetes.complications)
report_data <- diabetes.complications
report_data$fruitq1 <- factor(report_data$fruitq1, levels = c(0, 1),
                            labels = c("Other intake", "Low intake"))

curve <- cifcurve(Event(t, epsilon) ~ fruitq1, data = report_data,
                  outcome.type = "competing-risk")
cif_table <- tbl_survfit(curve, times = c(4, 8), type = "risk",
                         label_header = "**{time}-year CIF**")
cif_table
```

For competing risks, the `survfit`-compatible object stores `surv = 1 - CIF`.
The `type = "risk"` argument displays the CIF and reverses the saved interval
limits: the reported limits are `1 - upper` and `1 - lower`. The table does
not re-fit the curve or construct a different confidence interval.

## Selecting confidence intervals

Choose inference when fitting the curve. Here IF-based standard errors,
Student critical values and a log-log transformation are requested. For the
stored `1 - CIF`, this transformation is the complementary log-log
transformation of the CIF.

```{r student-intervals}
student_curve <- cifcurve(Event(t, epsilon) ~ fruitq1, data = report_data,
  outcome.type = "competing-risk", error = "if", conf.dist = "t",
  conf.type = "log-log")
student_table <- tbl_survfit(student_curve, times = c(4, 8), type = "risk",
  label_header = "**{time}-year CIF**") |>
  modify_footnote_header(columns = all_stat_cols(),
    footnote = "95% pointwise IF-t intervals; log-log transformation of 1 - CIF; deletion allocation for degrees of freedom.")
student_table
```

`error = "fay"` selects the Fay--Graubard-type variance correction, and
`df.method = "equal"` is an alternative allocation for IF-t. Supplied weights
are treated as fixed. Details of the inference methods are in `?cifcurve`.
Degrees of freedom vary by group and time; they are available in a summary
without adding diagnostic columns to the publication table.

```{r inference-diagnostics}
s <- summary(student_curve, times = c(4, 8), extend = TRUE)
data.frame(group = s$strata, time = s$time, df = s$df,
           interval_status = s$conf.status)
```

An unavailable interval remains missing. In particular, a valid interval is
not carried beyond the last positive-weight follow-up. Exact structural
boundaries retain the fitted singleton interval. These are pointwise
intervals, not simultaneous confidence bands.

## Comparing curves through a specified horizon

The following tests compare the CIF curves through 8 years. They are not
separate tests of the probabilities in each column of the preceding table.
The score tests emphasize earlier or later differences through their
Fleming--Harrington weights. The method labels are taken from the saved fits.

```{r curve-tests}
tests <- list(
  gray = ciftest(Event(t, epsilon) ~ fruitq1, report_data,
                 test = "gray", tau = 8),
  early = ciftest(Event(t, epsilon) ~ fruitq1, report_data,
                  test = "score", rho = 1, gamma = 0, tau = 8),
  late = ciftest(Event(t, epsilon) ~ fruitq1, report_data,
                 test = "score", rho = 0, gamma = 1, tau = 8)
)
test_results <- do.call(rbind, lapply(tests, function(fit) {
  x <- generics::tidy(fit)
  data.frame(method = paste(x$method, x$weight), p.value = x$p.value)
}))
test_table <- as_gtsummary(test_results) |>
  modify_header(method = "**Curve comparison through 8 years**",
                p.value = "**p-value**") |>
  modify_fmt_fun(p.value = label_style_pvalue(digits = 3))
test_table
```

This recipe reports the selected `ciftest()` results directly. The usual
`add_p()` default for a survival table is a log-rank test and does not select
these CIF tests. The ordinary Gray branch supports integer frequency
weights; it does not treat fractional IPTW as frequency weights.

To include the statistic and degrees of freedom, select `statistic` and
`parameter` from `generics::tidy(fit)`. The latter is the effective rank of
the test covariance, distinct from the time-specific Student degrees of
freedom used for the curve intervals.

## Labels and risk-set counts

Use gtsummary's existing label, header and formatting arguments to customize
the table. For a weighted fit, distinguish the number of observations,
the sum of weights and the effective sample size. `n.risk.type` chooses the
quantity exposed as `n.risk`; the legacy `n.risk`, `n.event` and `n.censor`
fields are rounded upward, while `n.risk.weighted`, `n.risk.unweighted` and
`n.risk.ess` retain their respective values on the native grid. An event count
in this curve object includes both event causes, not only retinopathy.

## Exporting the table

The table can be converted with standard gtsummary methods. The temporary
paths below can be replaced with the desired output filenames.

```{r export-cif}
html_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".html")
gt::gtsave(as_gt(student_table), filename = html_file)
```

```{r export-cif-word, eval=reporting_ready && requireNamespace('flextable', quietly=TRUE)}
word_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".docx")
flextable::save_as_docx(as_flex_table(student_table), path = word_file)
```
